subject: psychology
title: Research Methods: Sampling and Ethics
welcome_lead: Choose participants well and treat them ethically.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on sampling techniques and the BPS Code of Ethics.
final_note: You can pick the right sample and avoid ethical pitfalls.

concepts.def: Manipulates an independent variable to measure an effect.
Selecting a representative group from a population.
Consent, confidentiality and protection from harm.

walkthroughs.body_html: Random = unbiased but hard to organise. Stratified = representative but time-consuming. Opportunity = quick but biased. Volunteer = motivated participants but a self-selected sample.

Key principles: informed consent, right to withdraw, protection from harm, confidentiality, no unnecessary deception, and a thorough debrief. Researchers must weigh costs and benefits before going ahead.
A school study should: obtain parental consent, brief participants, allow withdrawal, anonymise data, and debrief afterwards. A pilot study can iron out problems before the main investigation.

mcqs.q: Picking the first 20 students who walk past you is:
Which ethical principle means knowing what the study involves before agreeing?
What does a correlation of -0.8 indicate?
options: A weak relationship (because it is negative).

mcqs.q: When is deception in research ever acceptable?
options: When demand characteristics would otherwise invalidate the study, with thorough debrief and ethics approval.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Volunteer sample”?
options: Whoever is available at the time.
Participants who reply to an advert.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “BPS Code”?
